The [[United Nations]] uses three definitions for what constitutes a city, as not all cities in all jurisdictions are classified using the same criteria. Cities may be defined as the [[city proper|cities proper]], their [[metropolitan area|metropolitan regions]], or the extent of their [[urban area]]. A complicating factor is that many large cities in the world have not only homeless or the unhoused, but also vast [[slum]] communities. This leads to official census data being less accurate in representing the actual number of residents in a given area.

==Definitions==
=== City proper (administrative unit) ===
{{Main|City proper}}
{{maplink|frame=yes|type=shape|stroke-width=2|id=Q11725|title=Chongqing|stroke-color=#000000|zoom=6|frame-lat=29.558|frame-long=107.50|frame-width=300|frame-height=240|frame-coordinates={{Coord|30|00|30|N|107|34|00|E|region:CN-50|display=it}}|type2=shape|stroke-width2=2|id2=Q40|title2=Austria|text=The municipality of [[Chongqing]], China, whose administrative jurisdictional area is approximately the size of [[Austria]], has the largest population of any [[city proper]]; however around 30% of its residents live in [[rural area]]s.}}
A city can be defined by its administrative boundaries, otherwise known as [[city proper]]. [[UNICEF]] defines city proper as, "the population living within the administrative boundaries of a city or controlled directly from the city by a single authority." A city proper is a locality defined according to legal or political boundaries and an administratively recognised urban status that is usually characterised by some form of [[local government]].<ref name=wup2007>{{cite web|url=http://esa.un.org/unup/index.asp?panel=6 |title=World Urbanization Prospects: The 2007 Revision Population Database |publisher=United Nations |access-date=26 July 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100822053414/http://esa.un.org/unup/index.asp?panel=6 |archive-date=22 August 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://millenniumindicators.un.org/unsd/demographic/sconcerns/densurb/densurbanNotes.htm |title=United Nations Statistics Division – Demographic and Social Statistics |publisher=United Nations |access-date=26 July 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110623192351/http://millenniumindicators.un.org/unsd/demographic/sconcerns/densurb/densurbanNotes.htm |archive-date=23 June 2011  }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=Demographic Yearbook 2005, Volume 57 |year=2008 |publisher=United Nations |isbn=978-92-1-051099-8 |page=241 |url = https://books.google.com/books?id=OwfGJtkpCbwC&pg=PA241 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160502022103/https://books.google.com/books?id=OwfGJtkpCbwC&pg=PA241 |archive-date=2 May 2016  }}</ref> Cities proper and their boundaries and population data may not include suburbs.<ref name=wup2003>{{cite book |title=World Urbanization Prospects: The 2003 Revision |year=2004 |publisher=United Nations |isbn=92-1-151396-0 <!-- This is the correct ISBN. The number on the copyright page of the book is invalid. --> |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=oxOAckK2stYC |access-date=13 February 2016 |archive-date=3 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200203051502/https://books.google.com/books?id=oxOAckK2stYC |url-status=live }}</ref>

The use of city proper as defined by administrative boundaries may not include suburban areas where an important proportion of the population working or studying in the city lives.<ref name=wup2003 /> Because of this definition, the city proper population figure may differ greatly from the urban area population figure, as many cities are amalgamations of smaller municipalities, and conversely, many Chinese cities govern territories that extend well beyond the core urban area into suburban and rural areas.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Alexander|first1=Ruth|title=The world's biggest cities: How do you measure them? |url = https://www.bbc.com/news/magazine-16761784|date=29 January 2012|work=BBC News|access-date=16 March 2015|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150302023557/http://www.bbc.com/news/magazine-16761784|archive-date=2 March 2015  }}</ref> The Chinese municipality of [[Chongqing]], which is the largest city proper in the world by population, comprises a huge administrative area of 82,403&nbsp;km<sup>2</sup>, around the size of [[Austria]]. However, around 30% of its 30-million population are agricultural workers living in a [[rural area|rural setting]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/magazine-16761784|title=Which is the world's biggest city?|first=Ruth|last=Alexander|work=BBC News|date=29 January 2012|access-date=21 July 2018|archive-date=2 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150302023557/http://www.bbc.com/news/magazine-16761784|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vuQRDAAAQBAJ&pg=PA83|title=China Dreams: 20 Visions of the Future|first=William A.|last=Callahan|date=12 April 2015|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=9780190235239|via=Google Books|access-date=21 September 2020|archive-date=16 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210616085517/https://books.google.com/books?id=vuQRDAAAQBAJ&pg=PA83|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2021年重庆市国民经济和社会发展统计公报 |url=https://tjj.cq.gov.cn/zwgk_233/fdzdgknr/tjxx/sjzl_55471/tjgb_55472/202203/t20220318_10522726_wap.html |website=重庆市统计局 |access-date=2026-07-13}}</ref>

=== Metropolitan area ===
{{Main|Metropolitan area}}
[[File:Night in the Greater Tokyo Area ISS054.jpg|thumb|[[Greater Tokyo Area|Tokyo]], the world's third-largest city by metropolitan population.]]
A city can be defined by the inhabitants of its [[demography|demographic]] population, as by [[metropolitan area]], or [[labour economics|labour market]] area. UNICEF defines metropolitan area as follows:

{{blockquote|A formal local government area comprising the urban area as a whole and its primary commuter areas, typically formed around a city with a large concentration of people (i.e., a population of at least 100,000). In addition to the city proper, a metropolitan area includes both the surrounding territory with urban levels of residential [[population density|density]] and some additional lower-density areas that are adjacent to and linked to the city (e.g., through frequent transport, road linkages or commuting facilities).}}

In many countries, metropolitan areas are established either as a local administrative organisation or only for statistical purposes. In the [[United States]], [[metropolitan statistical area]] (MSA) is defined by the [[United States Office of Management and Budget|U.S. Office of Management and Budget]] (OMB).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/sites/default/files/omb/assets/omb/bulletins/fy2009/09-01.pdf |last=Nussle |first=Jim |title=Update of Statistical Area Definitions and Guidance on Their Uses |publisher=Office of Management and Budget |date=Nov 20, 2008 |pages=1–2 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170121004705/https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/sites/default/files/omb/assets/omb/bulletins/fy2009/09-01.pdf |archive-date=2017-01-21 }}</ref> In the [[Philippines]], metropolitan areas have an official agency, such as [[Metropolitan Manila Development Authority]] (MMDA), which manages [[Metro Manila|Manila metropolitan area]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Home|url=https://mmda.gov.ph/|access-date=2021-06-16|website=mmda.gov.ph|archive-date=10 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210610035522/https://mmda.gov.ph/|url-status=live}}</ref> Similar agencies exist in [[Indonesia]], such as Jabodetabekjur Development Cooperation Agency for [[Jakarta metropolitan area]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://metro.tempo.co/read/1152868/3-masalah-utama-bksp-jabodetabekjur-yang-dipimpin-anies-baswedan|title=3 Masalah Utama BKSP Jabodetabekjur yang Dipimpin Anies Baswedan|first=Untung|last=Widyanto|date=6 December 2018|website=Tempo|access-date=11 April 2020|archive-date=9 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210309045755/https://metro.tempo.co/read/1152868/3-masalah-utama-bksp-jabodetabekjur-yang-dipimpin-anies-baswedan|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Urban area ===

{{Main|Urban area}}
A city can be defined as a conditionally [[Geographic contiguity|contiguous]] [[urban area]], with relatively less regard to territorial or administrative boundaries. [[UNICEF]] defines urban area as follows:

{{blockquote|The definition of "urban" varies from country to country, and, with periodic reclassification, can also vary within one country over time, making direct comparisons difficult. An urban area can be defined by one or more of the following: administrative criteria or political boundaries (e.g., area within the jurisdiction of a municipality or town committee), a threshold population size (where the minimum for an urban settlement is typically in the region of 2,000 people, although this varies globally between 200 and 50,000), population density, economic function (e.g., where a significant majority of the population is not primarily engaged in agriculture, or where there is surplus employment) or the presence of urban characteristics (e.g., paved streets, electric lighting, sewerage).}}

According to [[Demographia]], an urban area is a continuously built up land mass of urban development that is within a labor market (metropolitan area or metropolitan region) and contains no [[rural area|rural land]].

== List ==
{{For|more variety of estimates|Megacity#List of megacities}}

There are 85 cities in the world with a population exceeding 5 million people, according to 2025 estimates by the [[United Nations]].<ref name=UNpopulation>{{Cite web |url=https://www.un.org/development/desa/pd/sites/www.un.org.development.desa.pd/files/undesa_pd_2025_wup2025_summary_of_results.pdf |year=2025 |work=United Nations |location=New York |title=World Urbanization Prospects 2025 |access-date=20 November 2025 }}</ref>
